about.heading: Commercial lead with an engineer's eye.
paragraphs: I'm a D2C and eCommerce lead with a technical background. I started in Nestle IT - web security, hosting and CI for 30+ brand websites - moved into SEO and paid search for Purina, ran the Nestle Infant Nutrition eShop end to end, and since 2024 have owned the D2C channel for Ploom at JTI in Dubai.
That mix lets me speak the language of both brand teams and engineers: I set the commercial direction, write requirements developers can build from, and keep agencies and partners delivering on time.

jobs.title: D2C eShop Manager
bullets: Business owner of the ploom.ae D2C store launch (project May 2024 - Oct 2025): requirements, partner selection and contracts (payments, instalments, delivery), Adobe Commerce (Magento) platform, an OMS designed from scratch, integrations and the Arabic version. Live on the planned date together with Accenture and JTI IT.
Run the store end to end with a lean two-person team: trading, CRM, UX and operations.

Proposed and launched abandoned-cart recovery via email, SMS and WhatsApp with promo codes, Tabby instalments and custom OMS reports; helped configure and test the global Ploom Club loyalty and Refer a Friend programmes.
Since Feb 2026 also own paid media for the brand (programmatic and Meta).
Lead AI-visibility (GEO) work: monitoring how the brand appears in ChatGPT, Perplexity and other AI assistants.

freelance.heading: Freelance *web* work.
freelance.intro: Alongside my corporate career I have always built websites for small businesses. It started in 2017 as Extra Flow, a one-person studio: I talked to clients, designed the pages, built them on WordPress and set up analytics and SEO. Today I still take on the occasional project for people I know. The early work is simple by today's standards, but it is where I learned to ship a site end to end.
freelance.youtube: Screen recordings of these sites are also archived on the [Extra Flow YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/@extraflow4278).

lessons.title: The whole chain
lessons.text: Brief, design, build, launch, analytics, SEO. Doing every step myself is why I can write requirements engineers can build from today.

lessons.title: Sites exist to sell
lessons.text: Small business owners judge a site by calls and orders, not by looks. That lens carried straight into D2C eCommerce.

lessons.title: Things that last
lessons.text: Several of these sites are still running years later with little maintenance. Simple, well-structured builds age well.

meta.title: Ploom.ae D2C launch - case study - Mikhail Buzumurga
meta.description: How Mikhail Buzumurga led the launch of the ploom.ae direct-to-consumer store in the UAE as business owner: partners, OMS, integrations, Arabic version and a launch on the planned date.
meta.ogDescription: Launching a D2C store from zero in the UAE: partners, OMS, integrations, Arabic version - live on the planned date.

ploomCase.heading: Ploom.ae: a D2C store *from zero* to launch.
ploomCase.byline: Business owner · May 2024 - Oct 2025 · Live on the planned date
ploomCase.intro: Ploom needed its own direct-to-consumer store in the UAE. There were no local payment or delivery partners, no order management system and a fixed launch date. As business owner I set the requirements, chose the partners and kept every party moving to one date.

stats.label: the whole store in two languages
partners selected and contracted: payments, instalments, delivery

setup.heading: Many parties, *one date*.
paragraphs: The project brought together Accenture as the global agency, JTI global and local IT, partner companies and their developers, and internal legal and brand teams.
My job was to turn the brand's goals into requirements people could build from, make the decisions nobody else owned and keep everyone on one plan.

done.heading: Owned the launch end to end.

items.title: Partners and contracts
items.text: Found, shortlisted and selected the local partners, and negotiated contracts with the payment gateway (HyperPay), buy-now-pay-later (Tabby) and delivery (Swftbox).

items.title: Order management from scratch
items.text: Designed the OMS together with a developer: how orders flow, what every screen looks like, which reports and functions operations need.

items.title: Integrations
items.text: Connected the Adobe Commerce store with the OMS, payments and delivery, working between global IT, local IT and partner developers.

items.title: Arabic version
items.text: Ran the translation of the whole store from English into Arabic - a large volume of product, service and legal content.

items.title: Store features
items.text: Configured login, checkout and the rest of the storefront with IT and Accenture.

items.title: Processes
items.text: Set up how orders, deliveries and customer questions are handled day to day, so a small team can run the store.

beyond.heading: What I proposed and *pushed through*.
beyond.intro: Improvements that were not in the original scope:
items: Abandoned-cart recovery by email, SMS and WhatsApp
Promo codes for abandoned carts and unfinished orders
Order-status emails sent from the OMS, which the platform did not provide out of the box
Custom OMS reports by order and by SKU
Google Maps listings for the brand's shop-in-shops in malls
Dozens of smaller process and site fixes
beyond.note: Global programmes such as Ploom Club loyalty and Refer a Friend came from the brand's global team; I helped configure and test them for the UAE.

result.heading: Live on the planned date.
result.text: The store launched on the date set at the start of the project, with no delays. Today it runs with a two-person team, and since February 2026 I also own the brand's paid media.
